scope: Four already-discovered issues advanced; one scheduler-mechanism component execution and three source reviews.

scheduler_component.scope: Real CPU scheduler, upstream MockKVConnector and four metadata-only Requests; no LMCache runtime, model weights, GPU tensors, PD traffic or network transfer. Full-hit semantics controlled to match upstream issue discussion.
scheduler_component.attribution_limit: Explicit request-submission Task IDs and stacks are saved. This is not generic Task-birth capture, actual KV-object ownership or a validated CoroPerf diagnosis. No physical GPU allocation, transport saturation, retained-memory leak or indefinite stall is established.
scheduler_component.interpretation: A compute token budget does not cap this controlled asynchronous external-KV reservation path. This mechanism is consistent with the upstream scheduler discussion, but does not establish a broken compute-accounting contract or the original LMCache PD allocation retry. No baseline, fix or second run.

source_reviews.finding: PR3540 is closed unmerged. At its base 34de71775a32ac4cfda95854807e60fb31d8e017, StorageManager.async_lookup_and_prefetch has no num_computed_tokens argument. MP-mode fix claims are not proof the classic connector path is fixed.
source_reviews.coroperf_value: Quantify redundant reads by request/lookup Task, chunk intervals, APC computed-token boundary and actual bytes read; Task stacks alone do not determine GPU residency.

source_reviews.finding: PR1053 merged an event-driven completion branch, but its common.cmake defaults USE_EVENT_DRIVEN_COMPLETION to OFF and transfer_task.cpp retains the polling branch. This is a historical patch finding, not a claim about current wheels.
source_reviews.coroperf_value: A CPU profile already locates the busy poll. Additional value requires transfer/batch/request ownership and actual completion latency, plus the build configuration; no independent attribution validated.

source_findings: The Dec 25 follow-up already identifies createXferReq with no potential backend and carries request_id, operation_id and active-message id through the transfer logs. This is more specific than an unexplained disk-read wait.

At the reviewed v0.7.0 source, BlockTransferHandler marks connector-scheduled transfer handles complete for both Ok and Err. It acknowledges the active message regardless of the transfer result, so an ACK is not proof of transfer success.

Worker get_finished polls connector.is_complete per onboarding request. LocalOnboardTask logs process_onboard_request errors and keeps consuming. This does not by itself prove that errors are dropped before the scheduler slot, nor that the same path explains every reported hang.
source_reviews.coroperf_opportunity: Correlate request and operation IDs with actual Rust task identity, transfer terminal Result and request-slot state. Do not present generic Task stacks as a NIXL backend diagnosis; logs already carry substantial identity context.
source_reviews.blocker: Checked cached CPU vLLM environment has no kvbm, nixl, nixl-cu12 or ai-dynamo-runtime distribution. Matching old native bindings/transport/model are not ready. GPUs exist; no full serving, native build or mock substitute attempted.
